서른.forms: native · counting things, age · same before a counter (서른 살, 서른한 명)
서른.x: My older sister is thirty this year.
서른.e: Common for ages: 서른 살 = 30 years old.

소금.x: I added a little salt to the soup.

싸다.x: Fruit is cheap at the market.
싸다.e: 쌈 (lettuce wraps) comes from the other 싸다.
싸다.t: A different verb 싸다 means 'to pack, to wrap' (e.g. 짐을 싸다).

싸다.ex: 엄마가 아침마다 학교 도시락을 싸 주셨어요.
싸다.x: My mom packed my school lunch every morning.
싸다.e: Homonym warning: 싸다 also means 'cheap' — context tells you which.
싸다.t: Common collocations: 짐을 싸다 'pack bags', 도시락을 싸다 'pack a lunch', 선물을 싸다 'wrap a gift.'

전기.x: I turned off the light in my room to save electricity.

전기.ex: 어릴 때 위인 전기를 많이 읽었어요.
전기.x: When I was little, I read a lot of biographies of great people.
전기.t: 전기 also means 'electricity' (電氣) and 'first half' (前期); context tells you which.

베개.ex: 베개가 너무 높아서 잠을 잘 못 잤어요.
베개.x: My pillow was too high, so I didn't sleep well.
베개.e: From 베다 'to rest one's head on' + -개 (tool).

감사.ex: 도와주신 모든 분들께 깊은 감사를 드립니다.
감사.x: I offer my deep thanks to everyone who helped.
감사.t: 감사를 드리다 is the polite set phrase for 'to give thanks'; 감사합니다 is a bit more formal than 고맙습니다.

아나운서.ex: 그 아나운서는 뉴스를 아주 정확하게 읽어요.
아나운서.x: That announcer reads the news very accurately.
아나운서.e: From English 'announcer'; in Korean it usually means a broadcaster or news anchor.

벌금.x: If you park here, you'll have to pay a fine.

주의.ex: 눈이 와서 길이 미끄러우니까 주의가 필요해요.
주의.x: It snowed and the roads are slippery, so you need to be careful.
주의.t: Usually pronounced [주이]; don't confuse with 주의 主義 '-ism,' as in 민주주의.

벌레.x: In summer, bugs often come into the room.
벌레.e: Everyday word for any creepy-crawly; 곤충 is the scientific 'insect'.

개인.ex: 이 문제는 개인이 혼자 해결하기 어려워요.
개인.x: This problem is hard for an individual to solve alone.

위기.x: The company got through a major crisis.

판사.ex: 판사가 그 사람에게 벌금을 내라고 했어요.
판사.x: The judge ordered that person to pay a fine.

의도.x: I didn't mean it in a bad way.

렌즈.ex: 오늘은 안경 대신 렌즈를 끼고 왔어요.
렌즈.x: Today I came wearing contacts instead of glasses.
렌즈.t: In daily talk 렌즈 usually means contact lenses (콘택트렌즈). Put them in with 끼다, take them out with 빼다.

반전.ex: 그 영화는 마지막에 큰 반전이 있어요.
반전.x: That movie has a big twist at the end.
반전.t: 반전이 있다 = to have a twist; 반전 매력 = surprising charm, a popular casual expression.

유출.ex: 개인 정보 유출 사고가 또 일어났습니다.
유출.x: Another personal data leak has occurred.
유출.t: Common collocations: 정보 유출 'data leak', 기름 유출 'oil spill'.

민주주의.x: Elections are the most important part of democracy.
민주주의.t: Commonly pronounced [민주주이]; the possessive 민주주의의 is said [민주주이에].

좌절.x: Don't get discouraged just because you failed a few times.
좌절.e: Literally 'bent and snapped', like a branch breaking.
좌절.t: 좌절 is being crushed by failure, not everyday annoyance; for that, use 짜증.

친근하다.ex: 그 선생님은 학생들에게 친근하게 대해 주세요.
친근하다.x: That teacher treats students in a friendly way.

희망적.x: The doctor said the situation looks hopeful.
희망적.t: Pronounced [히망적] — ㅢ after a consonant sounds like ㅣ.

치밀하다.m: meticulous, thorough; (of plans) carefully worked out
치밀하다.ex: 그는 여행 계획을 아주 치밀하게 세웠어요.
치밀하다.x: He planned the trip very meticulously.
치밀하다.e: Literally 'fine and dense' — leaving no gaps.

유치하다.x: Please stop making such childish jokes now.
유치하다.t: A different 유치하다 means 'to attract' (investment, events), as in 올림픽을 유치하다.

유치하다.m: to attract (investment, tourists, events), to bring in
유치하다.ex: 우리 시는 올림픽을 유치하기 위해 노력하고 있어요.
유치하다.x: Our city is working to host the Olympics.
유치하다.e: Literally 'induce to come' — drawing in investment or events.
유치하다.t: Don't confuse with the adjective 유치하다 (childish), which uses different hanja.

염치.ex: 염치가 있으면 그런 부탁은 못 해요.
염치.x: If you had any sense of shame, you couldn't ask a favor like that.

무작정.x: I came up to Seoul blindly, without any plan.

가로채다.m: to intercept, to snatch; to steal (credit, an idea)
가로채다.ex: 동료가 제 아이디어를 가로채서 정말 화가 났어요.
가로채다.x: I was really angry because a coworker stole my idea.
가로채다.e: 가로 'sideways' + 채다 'to snatch': grabbing something from the side.
가로채다.t: 말을 가로채다 means to cut someone off mid-sentence.

타당성.ex: 전문가들이 그 계획의 타당성을 검토하고 있어요.
타당성.x: Experts are reviewing the feasibility of that plan.

그러다 보니.forms: A. 그러다 보니 B. · after verbs: -다 보니
그러다 보니.m: and so (over time), as a result of that
그러다 보니.ex: 매일 야근했어요. 그러다 보니 건강이 나빠졌어요.
그러다 보니.x: I worked late every day. And over time, my health got worse.
그러다 보니.e: 그러다 'to do so' + -다 보니 'as one keeps doing (one finds that)'.
그러다 보니.t: Shows a result that came gradually, often unplanned, from repeating something: 자주 만났어요. 그러다 보니 친해졌어요.

민의.m: will of the people, public will
민의.x: Politicians should follow the will of the people.
민의.t: 민의 is formal and means what people want; 민심 is more about their feelings and mood.

마음가짐.x: Start the new year with a fresh mindset.
마음가짐.e: From 마음 'heart, mind' plus 가지다 'to hold': how you hold your mind.

광복절.x: On Liberation Day, many homes hang out the Korean flag.

보전하다.ex: 우리는 자연을 잘 보전해서 후손에게 물려줘야 해요.
보전하다.x: We should preserve nature well and pass it on to future generations.
보전하다.t: 보전 keeps a living system intact (환경 보전); 보존 stores something unchanged (문화재 보존).

심사하다.m: to examine, to judge, to screen
심사하다.x: Experts judged the participants' works fairly.

희생적.ex: 어머니의 희생적인 사랑 덕분에 저는 공부를 마칠 수 있었어요.
희생적.x: Thanks to my mother's selfless love, I was able to finish my studies.
희생적.e: 희생 originally meant an animal offered in a ritual sacrifice.

우두커니.ex: 그는 아무 말 없이 문 앞에 우두커니 서 있었어요.
우두커니.x: He stood blankly in front of the door without a word.
우두커니.t: 물끄러미 is about looking; 우두커니 is about standing or sitting still.

하도.ex: 하도 피곤해서 수업 중에 잠이 들었어요.
하도.x: I was so tired that I fell asleep in class.
하도.e: Probably from Middle Korean 하다 'to be many, great'.
하도.t: Always followed by a reason clause like -아서/어서; it never ends a sentence on its own.

처분.m: disposal, getting rid of (property); punishment, disciplinary action
처분.ex: 그는 빚을 갚으려고 가지고 있던 땅을 처분했어요.
처분.x: He sold off the land he owned to pay his debts.
처분.e: Literally 'handling and dividing up' — deciding what happens to something or someone.
처분.t: In legal news, 처분 often means an official ruling or penalty, as in 행정 처분 'administrative action'.

연소.x: Carbon dioxide is released when wood burns.
연소.t: Homonym warning: 연소 (年少) means 'young in age', as in 최연소 'the youngest'.

가세하다.m: to join in, to side with, to add one's strength
가세하다.ex: 다른 회사들까지 가세하면서 가격 경쟁이 치열해졌습니다.
가세하다.x: As other companies joined in, the price competition grew fierce.

과실치사.ex: 트럭 운전자는 업무상 과실치사 혐의로 경찰에 입건되었습니다.
과실치사.x: The truck driver was booked by police on charges of negligent homicide in the course of work.
과실치사.e: Literally 'causing death by mistake' — killing through negligence, not intent.

불공정거래.ex: 금융 당국은 주식 불공정거래를 엄격하게 처벌합니다.
불공정거래.x: Financial authorities strictly punish unfair stock trading.

공명심.m: desire for fame and credit, ambition for glory
공명심.ex: 그는 공명심 때문에 무리하게 일을 추진했습니다.
공명심.x: He pushed the project too hard out of a desire for glory.
공명심.e: Literally 'a heart set on merit and a name.'
공명심.t: Usually negative: it suggests chasing credit rather than doing the right thing.

분산.ex: 분산이 크다는 것은 자료가 넓게 퍼져 있다는 뜻이에요.
분산.x: A large variance means the data is widely spread out.
분산.t: Outside statistics, 분산 means spreading out, as in 위험을 분산하다 (to spread risk).

헬륨.x: If you fill a balloon with helium, it floats up into the sky.

회절.ex: 소리는 회절 때문에 벽 뒤에서도 들립니다.
회절.x: Because of diffraction, sound can be heard even behind a wall.
회절.e: Literally 'turn and bend' — a wave bending around an obstacle.

문장력.ex: 책을 많이 읽으면 문장력이 자연스럽게 좋아져요.
문장력.x: If you read a lot, your writing ability naturally improves.
문장력.e: Literally 'sentence power'; -력 = ability: 필력, 표현력, 이해력.
문장력.t: Pronounced [문장녁] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

벌초.m: tidying ancestral graves (cutting the grass), grave weeding
벌초.ex: 추석 전에 가족들과 벌초를 하러 시골에 가요.
벌초.x: Before Chuseok, I go to the countryside with my family to tidy the graves.
벌초.e: Literally 'cutting grass' — done on family graves before Chuseok.
벌초.t: News often warns about bee stings and snakes during 벌초 season in late August and September.

발인.m: departure of the funeral procession, carrying out the coffin
발인.ex: 발인은 내일 아침 일곱 시에 있을 예정입니다.
발인.x: The funeral procession will depart tomorrow at 7 a.m.
발인.e: The moment the coffin leaves for burial or cremation, usually on day three.
발인.t: Funeral notices list 발인 with a date and time, so guests know when the procession leaves.

춘분.ex: 춘분에는 낮과 밤의 길이가 거의 같아요.
춘분.x: On the spring equinox, day and night are almost the same length.
춘분.e: Literally 'spring division' — day and night split evenly.

고수하다.m: to stick to, to adhere firmly to
고수하다.ex: 그 식당은 전통 방식을 고수하고 있어요.
고수하다.x: That restaurant sticks to the traditional way of doing things.
고수하다.e: Literally 'firmly guard' — refusing to let go.
고수하다.t: Homonym alert: 고수 can also mean an expert (高手) or cilantro.

실추되다.m: to be damaged, to fall (of reputation, authority)
실추되다.ex: 이번 사건으로 회사의 이미지가 크게 실추됐습니다.
실추되다.x: The company's image was badly damaged by this incident.
실추되다.t: Collocates with 명예, 위신, 신뢰, 이미지.

신묘하다.ex: 그 의사는 신묘한 의술로 이름이 났어요.
신묘하다.x: That doctor became famous for his marvelous healing skills.

자기검열.ex: 기자들은 외부 압력 때문에 자기검열을 하게 되었습니다.
자기검열.x: Under outside pressure, reporters ended up censoring themselves.

부언하다.m: to add (a remark), to say further

불가사의.x: The pyramids are one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
불가사의.e: Literally 'cannot be thought of or discussed'; originally a Buddhist term.
